regulator.notes: The issuer is the State of Israel through the Accountant General's Government Debt Management Unit; sales to the public go through banks and TASE members (GOV-10). Trading on TASE is under the ISA's supervision of the exchange (Securities Law ss.45, 51; REG-13). The account that holds the bonds is supervised separately: a bank by the Supervisor of Banks, a non-bank member by TASE (BRK-04). The site's copy has no name for the Finance Ministry as an issuer, so the regulator shown is the one over the market.

labels: accrued interest paid when buying between coupon dates is not modelled (TXI OQ5, G-10)

lawful_exit.text: Any trading day: a tradable series can be sold on TASE at the market price of the day (GOV-17). Held to maturity, the state redeems the face value in one payment, indexed for a CPI-linked series (GOV-11, GOV-15). An early redemption by the state is its option, by buyback at market price (GOV-16). The settlement cycle for a secondary sale was not readable (GOV open question 7), so no payout-days figure is recorded.

switch_is_tax_event.notes: Selling one series to buy another is a sale (s.88 "מכירה"): an unlinked series pays up to 15% on the whole gain (TXI-12), a CPI-linked series up to 25% on the real gain (TXI-14), withheld by the bank or member (TXS-05).

eligibility.text: any individual with a securities account at a bank or at a non-bank TASE member (BRK-32), buying a tradable series on TASE on any trading day (GOV-17); the bank's fee types for the trade follow its tariff (BRK-16). Sales to the public in the weekly auctions go by law through banks, TASE members and other approved bodies (GOV-10), but how a retail order reaches an auction, with what minimum and fee, was not found (GOV open question 8). The issue unit is NIS 1,000 face value (GOV-11, GOV-15); the TASE trading unit was not readable (GOV open question 7). Designated series (ערד, ח"ץ) are issued only to pension funds and insurers (GOV-18)

protection.text: principal and coupons are paid from the state's general revenues, an obligation of the state and not of the bank or broker (GOV-02). A CPI-linked series has no floor in the regulation text: if the index falls below the base index, principal and coupon are reduced (GOV-12; per-series floors unverified, GOV open question 6). A state buyback before maturity is at market price and the state's option (GOV-16). The paper sits in a securities account: at a non-bank TASE member client securities are held apart, in trust at the clearing house (BRK-07; REG open question 9); at a bank they are pooled through the nominee company and separated in its books (BRK-10, one bank's terms). What happens to client securities if a bank fails was not found (REG open question 10); a guarantee of a failing bank's deposits is discretionary (REG-06)
